chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his dog, so it seized a prey and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Eat from what the dog kills when you have named (Bismillah) over it. So if you were forgetful, eat from it as well, and eat its remains.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating prey caught by a dog if the owner forgot to say Bismillah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the permissibility of consuming game caught by a hunting dog, emphasizing that the recitation of *Bismillah* at the time of sending the dog is the primary condition. Notably, the Imam permits eating even if the recitation was forgotten, highlighting the principle of ease in dietary laws, and explicitly allows consuming the 'leftovers' (*fadl*) of the prey, a detail that distinguishes this ruling from general slaughter practices. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the specific conditions of *dhikr* in hunting, contrasting with the stricter requirements often applied to animal slaughter.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moala Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about a man who sent his dog, so it seized a prey and ate from it. Can he eat from its remains?’ So heasws said: ‘Eat from what the dog kills when you Named (Bismillah) over it. So if had forgotten (Bismillah), so eat from it as well, and eat its remains’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from Mansur ibn Hazim from Salim al-Ashal who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about dog trained for hunting which has eaten of the prey.
He (the Imam) said, ‘You can use it (the prey) for food.”’
